page: Vultr vhf-4c-16gb is a virtual server belonging to the High Frequency Compute family. It features 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel x86_64 cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by a bundled 384 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall into the average range. Memory bandwidth tests reveal a significant performance tradeoff: while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 497.33 GB/sec, uncached large-block read and write bandwidths are weak, scoring in the bottom 25% at 35.47 GB/sec and 17.49 GB/sec respectively. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression are weak, though single-threaded bzip3 decompression remains average.

In application-level benchmarks, the server achieves average performance in Redis SET operations (6.0 million operations per second) and small model LLM text generation. However, it exhibits weak performance in database operations, static web serving, and prompt processing. Medium model LLM text generation is poor, scoring in the bottom 10%. Given the shared CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for general-purpose workloads, development environments, and lightweight caching layers that benefit from fast local NVMe storage but do not require sustained, dedicated multi-core compute resources.
